comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body:
=== gc-corruption fix (LANDED) + tickets-repo growth brainstorm (HANDOFF) ===

PART 1 — CI failure debug + fix (COMPLETE, landed on main):
- Root cause (proven, git 2.54): git>=2.47 `git commit` spawns a DETACHED `git maintenance run
  --auto` (repack --cruft --write-midx) that runs OUTSIDE rebar's write lock, racing concurrent
  writers on the shared linked-worktree object DB -> corruption (invalid object / Error building
  trees) -> dropped writes. rebar's lock is sound (0 overlaps). gc.auto=0 does NOT fix it
  (git>=2.47 gates on maintenance.auto, not gc.auto). Prior session's conclusion (py3.11-only;
  heal in delete_events) was WRONG.
- Fix: _gc_config_unit forces auto-gc FOREGROUND (gc.autoDetach=false + maintenance.autoDetach
  =false; gc.auto unset). Landed Gerrit 774 (MERGED). Temp skip 768 (merged->superseded).
  ADR 0051. Bug 88eb CLOSED+certified. Idea 341a (future posture: disable gc task, use
  loose-objects + geometric incremental-repack to bound per-run cost).

PART 2 — Tickets-repo unbounded-growth (measured facts, brainstorm ONGOING):
- Repo = 443 MB / ~178k objects for ~15k tickets. PACKED SIZE: blobs 424MB (95.7%),
  trees 10.7MB (2.4%), commits 8.2MB (1.8%). => tree churn / directory structure / sharding /
  active-archive split are the WRONG lever for SIZE (git deltas trees to ~0; sharding measured
  to INCREASE object count 2.00->3.00 trees/commit).
- Blob breakdown: .bridge_state = 375 MB (~85%): bindings.json 219MB/987 versions +
  prev_snapshot.json 155MB/4450 versions (full Jira snapshot up to 3.37MB/version, poor delta).
  Actual ticket/event blobs ~35 MB, slow growth.
- .bridge_state = reconciler Jira-sync cache. OPERATOR CORRECTION: it is CRITICAL, REQUIRED
  Jira infrastructure — do NOT propose removing it. My "stop versioning it" framing was
  rejected. New session must FIRST understand reconciler requirements (ADR 0026 three-way-merge
  -baseline, ADR 0027 binding lifecycle, WU-3 .gitattributes merge=ours) before any proposal.
- verify-identity whole-store scan cost: OWNED BY ANOTHER SESSION now; out of scope.

CONSTRAINTS: readers list the WORKTREE not history; cross-clone sync = union-merge of tickets
branch (any history checkpoint must be deterministic + re-applied on merge — git-annex forget
model); single-writer write lock; every write auto-commits+auto-pushes to origin/tickets.
Watch: events may bind trust to commit identity (signatures/attestations) — a squash/re-root
rewrites commit SHAs and could break those; must verify before any history rewrite.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body:
=== Growth prior-art research (how high-commit-volume git projects bound growth) ===

rebar's shape (append-only 1-commit-per-event branch, readers use worktree, clones sync by
union-merge) == a package-registry git index. That class hit this at scale; findings:

CONVERGENT INDUSTRY ANSWER = move the hot/high-churn data OFF shared git history onto HTTP/CDN:
- crates.io index: squashed history periodically (every 3-6 mo / at ~50-100k commits; archived
  old history to a separate crates.io-index-archive repo; deleting old branches matters because
  the server deltas master only against master). Team called shallow/squash "only temporary
  solutions"; real fix = sparse HTTP index (RFC 2789). git-as-high-commit-log deemed wrong tool.
- Homebrew 4.0.0: abandoned git taps, moved metadata to JSON over formulae.brew.sh; shallow
  clone was BANNED (server-hostile: incremental fetch into shallow recomputes trees).
- CocoaPods: Specs.git -> CDN. Go modules: HTTP proxy + Merkle-tile checksum log (never git).

CONSUMER-SIDE git tools (shallow, partial clone blob:none/tree:0, commit-graph, sparse-index,
git maintenance): reduce CLIENT cost only; NONE shrink the authoritative server store; treeless
partial clone RAISES server pack-objects CPU ~4x. Buys time, not a bound.

PRODUCER-SIDE (actually shrink the store):
- Periodic squash/re-root (crates.io) — shrinks; breaks pinned SHAs; needs archive + cadence bot.
- git replace --graft + filter-repo re-root — shrinks; rewrites ALL later commit SHAs; force-push
  + re-clone; disables commit-graph while grafts exist. filter-repo author calls periodic
  truncation "a bad usecase" but supports it.
- git-annex `forget` — THE closest analog: prunes a UNION-MERGED metadata branch's history;
  designed to survive UNCOORDINATED squash because union-merge re-converges different squash SHAs
  automatically (branch carries CONTENT not SHA-bound identity). Caveat: all clones need a
  supporting version; breaks if trust is bound to commit SHAs.
- Sapling/Mononoke segmented changelog (lazy history: don't shrink, stop transferring) + Dolt
  prolly-trees (size scales with changes not versions) — both require replacing git's object
  model, not layering on it.

VERDICT: (1) if a central read surface is acceptable -> serve current worktree state over
HTTP/CDN, history becomes internal/audit. (2) if distributed union-merge sync is non-negotiable
(rebar's case) -> periodic union-merge-SAFE squash/forget (crates.io cadence + git-annex
convergence), PROVIDED events don't bind trust to commit SHAs. (3) per-entity refs / lazy history
bound growth but replace the substrate.

FOR REBAR SPECIFICALLY: growth is 85% .bridge_state (a REGENERABLE cache). The industry pattern
for high-churn derived cache is NOT to keep it in shared history — but operator says it's
required, so the open question is whether its CURRENT state (required) can be retained without
its full HISTORY (219MB bindings.json/987 + 155MB prev_snapshot/4450), given the reconciler's
3-way-merge-baseline + binding-lifecycle needs. Understand those needs FIRST.

Full cited report in the session transcript (crates.io RFC 2789, git-annex forget docs, Homebrew
4.0.0, nesbitt.io "package managers keep using git as a database").

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body:
=== SESSION 3: bridge_state growth — reconciler-requirements investigation (VERIFIED) ===

CORRECTION of an earlier framing: prev_snapshot.json is NOT functionally redundant. Do NOT delete it.
Established by two independent adversarial subagents (red-team hunt-the-breaker + blue-team prove-removable)
that CONVERGED, plus direct code reads.

WHAT'S TRUE:
- prev_snapshot's DIRECTION-ARBITRATION role IS fully replaced by the per-binding baseline in bindings.json.
  PROVEN empirically, not just by reasoning: rollout ticket a118-fa8e recorded 30 consecutive zero-divergence
  shadow passes + a byte-identical flip pass; d6bd-95c9 hardcoded baseline-consumer-swap always-on; baseline-path
  direction tests pass (tests/.../diffing/test_baseline_arbitration.py::test_dryrun_arbitration_pinned_to_baseline
  feeds a STALE prev_snapshot and asserts the baseline wins). outbound_differ.py:795 -> outbound_fields.py:416-418
  overrides arbitration_prev = get_baseline(local_id); the prev_snapshot arg there is a fixture-only fallback = DEAD in prod.
- BUT arbitration is only 1 of ~6 consumers. prev_snapshot is STILL LOAD-BEARING as the EDGE-TRIGGER ANCESTOR:
  run_differs.py:198 calls differ.compute_mutations(prev_snapshot, curr_snapshot) UNCONDITIONALLY every pass;
  differ.py:299 "key in jira_state only -> inbound create". Empty prev => every Jira key looks new => re-emits the
  documented "2050+ inbound_create mutations on every pass" regression (reconcile.py:662-669). The baseline CANNOT
  cover this (keyed by local_id, confirmed-bindings only, no representation of UNBOUND native Jira issues).
- Other live prev_snapshot consumers with NO baseline equivalent: dual-identity invariant
  check_dual_identity_complete (run_differs.py:265, invariants.py); edge/level adoption coordination
  (binding_walk.py:205-212 skip_adopt_keys); corrupt-merge safety canary (_handle_corrupt_snapshot,
  reconcile.py:715-773 — also a tickets-branch-partial-merge tripwire); bridge_fsck drift oracle
  (bridge_fsck.py:257-291). NOTE: d6bd's stated keep-reason ("needed to seed baselines") is STALE —
  _advance_baselines reads curr not prev (reconcile.py:928) and seed_baselines_from_snapshot is never called in src/.

WHY IT'S STILL THE GROWTH DRIVER: prev_snapshot stores the FULL ACLI payload per issue (fetcher.py:413 + parent/
comment/issuelinks enrichments) — volatile fields (updated/created/watches/worklog) tick constantly across ~2050
issues => a new committed version nearly every pass (~4450 versions/155MB). Serialization is ALREADY canonical
(sort_keys+indent=2, dict-keyed) — reformatting buys nothing. It's advanced UNCONDITIONALLY every pass
(shutil.copy2 at reconcile.py:1008, no change-guard).

THE LEVER (verified-safe direction): prev_snapshot is OVER-PROVISIONED, not redundant. Its live consumers need at
most {key-set + rebar-id label + possibly the 5 mirrored fields}, NOT the full payload. So: NARROW the persisted
content to what the edge-trigger/dual-identity/fsck actually read (drops per-version size ~10-100x AND kills the
volatile-field churn that mints a version/pass) + CHANGE-GATE the advance. No delete, no history rewrite, no new ref,
no consumer broken. Open sizing question being verified now: is the legacy differ's key-in-both FIELD-DRIFT output
redundant with the outbound/classify path (=> prev shrinks to key->{rebar-id} map) or authoritative (=> retain 5 fields)?
Also a clean separate win: remove the DEAD outbound_differ prev_snapshot plumbing (OutboundDiffConfig.prev_snapshot
:364, :526, :795 threading, outbound_fields.py:416 fallback).

COORDINATION / SCOPE: bridge_state SIZE is UNOWNED. Active other session = epic 58b0 (comment/inbound-link SYNC
CORRECTNESS) — orthogonal to size, but shares the differ/field contract, so coordinate on any snapshot-content change.
Epic 6c9c-811f (dust-troth-naval, CLOSED) settled the storage posture: coordination state (pass/phase lock) moved to
refs/reconciler/*, but .bridge_state stays committed on the tickets branch with merge=ours as a derived cache
(WS-1 "re-home binding DATA off-branch" was EXPLICITLY DROPPED). So a separate-ref for bindings revives a dropped
decision; a separate self-resetting ref is viable ONLY for prev_snapshot (single ephemeral-CI writer, no non-reconciler
reader) but is dominated by simply narrowing it. bindings.json (219MB/987 versions) MUST stay on-branch — read by
ordinary clones via _ids.py:61 (Jira-key resolution) — its history bounding is a separate, lower-urgency problem.

DEFERRED (user parked pending this investigation): (1) how to keep a BOUNDED debug-history trail; (2) the existing
~337MB already sunk in history — accept + CI --filter=blob:none partial-clone (zero-risk) vs one-time reconciler-paused
all-clones-converged filter-repo reclaim (needs lockstep enforce_since re-pin rebar.toml:105 + flag-day force-push;
sync.py:90-92 --allow-unrelated-histories union DRAGS old blobs back from any un-converged peer, so periodic rewrite
is BROKEN, one-time only). Trust model survives a clean rewrite (ancestry-based, sigs cover event content-hash not
commit SHA — authorship.py) EXCEPT the enforce_since absolute SHA pin.
